name: synthetic-rag-reference
description: Synthetic Golden Dataset over the documentation of a fictional product, Aurora Cloud Storage. It covers eight RAG scenarios for smoke tests and offline CI; every fact is invented and self-contained.

samples.question: How many availability zones does Aurora Cloud Storage replicate each object to by default?
contexts: By default, Aurora Cloud Storage replicates every object to three availability zones within the primary region. Cross-region replication is an opt-in feature billed separately.
samples.ground_truth: By default, Aurora Cloud Storage replicates every object to three availability zones within the primary region.

samples.question: What is the maximum size of an object uploaded with a single PUT request?
contexts: A single PUT request can upload an object of up to 5 GiB. Objects larger than 5 GiB must use multipart upload, which supports objects of up to 5 TiB.
samples.ground_truth: A single PUT request can upload an object of up to 5 GiB; larger objects of up to 5 TiB must use multipart upload.

samples.question: Which storage class should a team use for compliance archives that are read less than once a year?
contexts: Compliance archives must use a storage class that supports Object Lock. Only the Standard and Glacier-Deep classes support Object Lock.
The Glacier-Deep class is designed for data accessed less than once a year and has a minimum storage duration of 180 days.
samples.ground_truth: Compliance archives must use a storage class that supports Object Lock, such as Glacier-Deep. The Glacier-Deep class is designed for data accessed less than once a year.

samples.question: Can deleted objects be recovered after the retention window ends?
contexts: Deleted objects remain recoverable from the trash for 30 days. After the 30-day retention window ends, deleted objects cannot be recovered.
samples.ground_truth: No. After the 30-day retention window ends, deleted objects cannot be recovered.

samples.question: When does the legacy v1 API stop accepting requests?
contexts: The legacy v1 API is deprecated and will stop accepting requests on 31 March 2027. Clients must migrate to the v2 API before that date.
samples.ground_truth: The legacy v1 API will stop accepting requests on 31 March 2027.

samples.question: Which authentication methods does the Aurora API support?
contexts: The Aurora API supports three authentication methods: API keys, OAuth 2.0 client credentials, and short-lived tokens issued by the identity service.
samples.ground_truth: The Aurora API supports API keys, OAuth 2.0 client credentials, and short-lived tokens issued by the identity service.

samples.question: How do I rotate an API key without downtime?
contexts: To rotate an API key without downtime, create a new key, deploy it to all clients, and then revoke the old key. Revoking a key takes effect within 60 seconds.
samples.ground_truth: Create a new key, deploy it to all clients, and then revoke the old key.

samples.question: How does the Standard class differ from the Infrequent-Access class in retrieval cost?
contexts: The Standard class has no retrieval fee and is intended for frequently accessed data.
The Infrequent-Access class charges a retrieval fee of $0.01 per GB in exchange for a lower monthly storage price.
samples.ground_truth: The Standard class has no retrieval fee. The Infrequent-Access class charges a retrieval fee of $0.01 per GB.
